clue.text: Clergyman departs for Pacific capital with least rainfall

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, so departs replaces the Pacific letter

parts.note: a priest is a member of the clergy

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, here the head of Pacific

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A minister leaves for the capital of a Pacific state that has the lowest rainfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city but means the first letter, P; 'for' then puts D in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of dry describes the place that gets the smallest amount of rain.

clue.text: Endless jam required by head of the household

indicators.note: what is needed by the head comes after it, so the jam piece follows

parts.note: dome is slang for the head

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off the word for jam

parts.note: to stick is to jam, as a drawer does

explanation.surface: A jam that never ends needs the attention of whoever runs the home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the K from STICK; 'required by' only joins the pieces, with DOME first.
explanation.definitionFit: Domestic is the adjective for things belonging to the home and family life.

clue.text: Temporary home one found in time

parts.note: at home is in, as in staying in

indicators.note: the letter for one is located inside the word for time

parts.note: a term is a period of time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A short-term residence is discovered within a set period.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim arrangement is a stopgap, lasting only until something permanent comes.

clue.text: Son becoming less excited about start of higher education

indicators.note: the cooling word goes round the extra letter

parts.note: cooling down is calming, losing excitement

indicators.note: only the first letter of higher is used

explanation.surface: A son calms down at the beginning of his time at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts H, from 'start of higher', inside COOLING, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is the teaching a person receives, a synonym for formal instruction.

clue.text: Artificial pitch of latest ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some unnatural musical note comes from the newest pulverised stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is the past tense of grind, telling you to rearrange OF LATEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is a man's voice pushed above its natural register, an unnatural singing pitch.

clue.text: Tailor may destroy suit with this, we hear

indicators.note: to tailor something is to cut and refashion it, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A tailor might ruin a suit using this, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailor' looks like the person making the suit but is the instruction to rework MAY DESTROY SUIT; 'we hear' is part of the definition, not a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear and nerve pathways that let us perceive sound form our hearing apparatus.

clue.text: Excessive energy in course of action

indicators.note: the energy letter sits within the word for action

parts.note: a step is a measure taken, a course of action
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Too much effort goes into a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside STEP after its T.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep price is unreasonably high, so it means too much.

clue.text: Dog almost swallowing new dish

indicators.note: the shortened dog takes the new letter inside it
the last letter of the dog is dropped

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog nearly gulps down a fresh plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TERRIER to TERRIE, and 'swallowing' takes N in before its last E.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrine is a pâté-like preparation, also the earthenware vessel it is cooked in.

clue.text: Nervous individual with degree appearing regularly

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: only every other letter of degree shows, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: An anxious person has a qualification that keeps turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of degree: D, G, E.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on edge is an idiom for being tense and jumpy.

clue.text: Sweet person not wanted by Charlie

parts.note: a gooseberry is British slang for an unwanted third person with a couple
a charlie is British slang for a fool or idiot

explanation.surface: A kind person is unwelcome to a man named Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the third wheel on a date is said to 'play gooseberry', and a 'right charlie' is a silly person.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseberry fool is a pudding of stewed fruit folded into cream, so a dessert.

clue.text: Fellow comes to court and daughter shivers

parts.note: a fellow is an equal or counterpart, a match
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A man arrives to woo a woman and her daughter trembles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivers' is not trembling but a noun: fragments, as in 'smashed to shivers'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivers are splinters, and matchwood is wood broken into tiny fragments.

clue.text: Always wanting volume that is spine-chilling

indicators.note: lacking, so the volume letter is removed

parts.note: ever means always
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone forever short of a book finds that frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic contraction of 'ever', which is why 'Always' without a volume still means always.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is uncanny and frightening enough to send a shiver down your back.

clue.text: Current in watery grave

indicators.note: the current letter goes inside the watery word

parts.note: serous describes thin watery bodily fluid
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A stream flows into a drowned man's tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place in the surface but is the adjective; 'in' puts I inside SEROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and serious are both adjectives for something solemn or weighty.

clue.text: A1 murder

definitions.meaning: killing, especially by hanging in British slang

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British: 'topping' as old-fashioned praise, and 'to top' someone as to kill them.
explanation.definitionFit: Topping is British slang both for excellent and for an execution or killing.

clue.text: A storage unit with two round feet

indicators.note: the two letters go round the others, one on each side

parts.note: II is the Roman numeral two
MB is the megabyte, a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: A cupboard with two circular legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps II around AMB, putting one I on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi, plural of iambus, are metrical units in verse, each a short then long syllable.

clue.text: Row about empty school in Yorkshire town

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes round the school letters

parts.note: a barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel

indicators.note: the inside of school is removed, keeping its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dispute concerns an abandoned school in a northern English town.
explanation.walkthrough: A barney is everyday British slang for a noisy row; 'empty' keeps only the ends of school.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnsley is a former mining town in South Yorkshire.

clue.text: Marine creature in hurricane's swimming right away

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are moving around, so they are rearranged
the right letter is removed from the storm word

parts.note: the word is taken with its S as fodder

explanation.surface: A sea animal is caught swimming in a storm with its right side gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' takes one R from HURRICANES, and 'swimming' rearranges the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a spiny marine invertebrate found on rocky sea beds.

clue.text: Repeating expression of surprise about school as a figure of speech

indicators.note: the doubled exclamation goes round the school
the exclamation is said twice

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone keeps exclaiming in surprise at a school treated as a metaphor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repeating' gives MYMY and 'about' puts ETON after its first M.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy is a rhetorical device naming a thing by something associated with it, as 'the Crown'.

clue.text: Furniture getting tossed about in steerage

indicators.note: thrown around, so the letters of steerage are rearranged

explanation.surface: Furniture is being thrown around in the cheap quarters of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed about' rearranges STEERAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Étagères are shelved stands for ornaments, a type of furnishing.

clue.text: Expel all the voters

definitions.meaning: to throw out or evict someone
the number of people who cast a ballot

explanation.definitionFit: To turn out is to eject, and an election's turnout is the people who voted.

clue.text: Award from Paris is big in New York

definitions.meaning: in Greek myth Paris gave a golden fruit as the prize to Aphrodite
New York City is nicknamed the Big ...

explanation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince of myth, not the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris awarded the golden fruit to the fairest goddess, and New York's nickname is the Big Apple.

clue.text: Drink after crew stops working

indicators.note: the drink word comes after the crew word

parts.note: a pack is a gang or crew
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Once the crew have had a drink, the work stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that packs up breaks down, an idiom for ceasing to function.

clue.text: Give up after a Conservative's come to office

indicators.note: the giving-up word comes after the other two pieces

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
to cede is to surrender or give up

explanation.surface: Someone resigns after a Tory has taken power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts CEDE behind A and C.
explanation.definitionFit: To accede to a throne or post is to take it up, entering a position of authority.

clue.text: Restaurant providing fish with tail removed so

indicators.note: the last letter of the fish is cut off

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: An eatery serves fish with the tail cut off, like this.
explanation.walkthrough: A carvery is a British pub or restaurant serving roast joints sliced at a counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is a British eatery where roast meat is carved to order, a type of restaurant.

clue.text: Father leaves new student somewhere in Surrey

indicators.note: the father abbreviation departs from the student word

parts.note: a fresher is a first-year university student in Britain
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A father walks out on a first-year student somewhere south of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes FR from FRESHER. Surrey is a county south-west of London; Esher is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a commuter town in Surrey, so a place in that county.

clue.text: Wind is back, taking big bird to outskirts of Chicago

indicators.note: the word is is read backwards

parts.note: the roc is a giant mythical bird

indicators.note: only the outer letters of Chicago are kept

explanation.surface: The Windy City wind is back as a giant bird reaches the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI; 'outskirts of Chicago' gives C and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa over the Mediterranean.

clue.text: It's hard to get by when coming back for an extended period

indicators.note: the word for get by is read in reverse

parts.note: to cope is to manage, to get by
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Making ends meet is tough when you return after a long time away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is only a link; 'when coming back' turns the get-by word, and the hard letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era, a long and distinct span of time.

clue.text: Clumsy TV hero, say, not looking before leaping

indicators.note: something clumsy is awkwardly put together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bungling television hero, for example, acts without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsy' rearranges TV HERO SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting too quickly without caution is the meaning of the proverb about looking before you leap.

clue.text: All books in republic? Only fifty per cent

indicators.note: the books letters go inside the republic

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

indicators.note: half of the word only is taken, here its last two letters

explanation.surface: Are all the books in a republic? Only half of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the republic is Ireland; 'fifty per cent' takes the second half of Only.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly or completely, an adverb for in full.

clue.text: Quick sort of dresser

definitions.meaning: a smart, stylish dresser is called a ... dresser

explanation.definitionFit: Snappy means brisk, and a snappy dresser is a stylish one.
